summary.headline: Amber H1 FY27 revenue up 28% to ₹6,515 crore; Q2 revenue up 60% to ₹2,627 crore, but Q2 adjusted loss of ₹57 crore on consumer durables margin pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to ₹2,627 crore, with operating EBITDA up 30% to ₹127 crore after ₹13.5 crore of inventory PPA adjustment. H1 revenue grew 28% to ₹6,515 crore and operating EBITDA 29% to ₹464 crore. Adjusted PAT was a loss of ₹57 crore in Q2 before a ₹9.5 crore exceptional loss, and H1 adjusted PAT was ₹269 crore before a ₹132.2 crore exceptional item. Consumer durables margins were hit by commodity inflation, forex, minimum wage revision and new-plant ramp-up costs, while the electronics division grew 94% with Q2 EBITDA of ₹116 crore. Management maintained the 50-100 bps consumer durables margin impact guidance but cut railways revenue growth guidance to 15-20%.

segments.name: Consumer durables (room AC)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹127 crore (+41% YoY) with operating EBITDA of ₹4 crore; margins hit by commodity prices, forex, minimum wage revision and ramp-up costs at the new Sidwal/Greenfield plant. Blended price increase of about 8% in Q2 YoY per management.

segments.name: Electronics (Ilin and subsidiaries)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹1,248 crore (+94% YoY) and operating EBITDA ₹116 crore (+195% YoY). Management would not split organic vs inorganic growth or PCB vs EMS revenue, citing the DRHP.

segments.name: Railway systems and defence
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹152 crore (+15% YoY) and operating EBITDA ₹7 crore; some fixed-price contracts absorbed commodity inflation. FY27 margin guided at about 2-10% (transcript unclear), normalising to about 4% later.

guidance_outlook: Consumer durables: margin impact of 50-100 bps retained for FY27, assuming commodities stay at H1 levels; further commodity spikes would suppress margins.
Margin recovery expected from Q3 as the remaining 50% of Q2 commodity increase is passed to customers; normalisation targeted by Q4 for conversion costs.
Railway systems and defence: FY27 revenue growth cut to 15-20%, lower than earlier expectations, due to delayed project offtakes.
Group revenue target of doubling top line in two years reiterated.
Capex of ₹1,800-2,000 crore for FY27 and similar range in FY28; interest cost expected flat at around ₹56-64 crore net per quarter for next two quarters.
Electronics capacity: Ascent Hosur expansion by H1 CY27; Kopran/Korea circuit expansion in CY28 per DRHP.
capex_capacity: Ascent Circuits Hosur expansion expected to start by H1 calendar 2027.
Korea circuit expansion expected to start in calendar 2028.
Sidwal Greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, doors and gangways) is operational; capacity utilisation reported around 40%.
Ilin fire-affected facility has resumed operations; SFG expected fully operational in a couple of months.
FY27 capex of ₹1,800-2,000 crore, similar range in FY28; PLI-type incentive cash flows expected from FY27-FY29 after commercial production.
demand_pricing: Consumer durables: management expects industry growth of about 20-22% for CY/FY and says Amber is in line; H1 industry growth cited at 18%. Management declined to disclose volume growth.

Commodity exposure in room AC BOM: copper, aluminium, steel, resin and USD; about 40% direct BOM exposure, rising to about 52% including raw-material-level exposure (e.g., compressor steel and copper).
Price pass-through: blended price increase of about 8% in Q2 YoY for RAC, net of supplier cost improvement against roughly 12% commodity inflation.
Legacy fixed-price contracts without price variation clauses are a margin drag; new contracts are being negotiated at new commodity levels.
Normalised consumer durables EBITDA margin expected to be gradual, around 14-16% over time, rather than the earlier 19-20%.
PCB/CCL shortage expected to ease over next two to three quarters as CCL capacity expands.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of electronics organic growth (about 35%) and how is commodity exposure split for RAC?
qa_highlights.answer: Electronics organic/inorganic split and job-order vs gross revenue treatment were not discussed due to the DRHP. For RAC, about 40% of BOM is commodity-exposed, 52% including raw-material level; electronics exposure is to CCL, ICs, memory, resins and transformers.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 41% consumer durables growth, and what was volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commercial AC contribution, star-rating and commodity-linked price changes, and volume growth; volume growth was not disclosed. Industry growth is expected at 20-22% for the year, with H1 industry at 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-offs and underlying margin in consumer durables?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-operating forex-related costs of about ₹32 crore in H1 at standalone level, plus minimum wage revision of about ₹22-25 crore and CCT2 plant extra costs of about ₹15-20 crore; total H1 one-offs about ₹80-85 crore. Margin recovery expected from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the electronics margin pressure ease and what about the doubling of revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins improved as commodity cost pass-through started with customers; management said the pressure is partially behind them, but it depends on future commodity and currency moves. Doubling the top-line target in two years is still intact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net interest cost was ₹56 crore in Q1 and ₹63-64 crore in Q2; similar levels expected for the next two quarters. Gross debt about ₹4,100-4,200 crore, net debt ₹2,572-2,582 crore, with seasonal peaks in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Ilin IPO and dilution affect Amber's control?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DRHP figures are at maximum dilution from CCPS conversions; ultimate dilution could be below 40%, and Amber expects to keep above 51% control. CB approval expected in 3-4 months, with a one-year window to launch the IPO.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, steel, USD, oil) and further pass-through lag could keep consumer durables margins suppressed.
Legacy fixed-price contracts without price variation clauses in consumer durables and railways.
Ilin fire-related operational impact and insurance recovery still being finalised; ₹6.3 crore difference recognised as exceptional loss.
Inventory PPA adjustment of about ₹32 crore remaining to be absorbed over the next two quarters.
Ilin IPO timing and Amber's stake dilution potentially below 51%; DRHP restricts disclosure on electronics segment.
Delays in railway project offtakes leading to cut in FY27 growth guidance.
Q2 consumer durables EBITDA of ₹4 crore; recovery to historical margins depends on Q3/Q4 pass-through.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth story and the electronics ramp, but evasive on segment, volume, PCB, Unitronics and IPO-related questions, citing the DRHP and listing constraints. Cautious on consumer durables margins, which management frames as temporary and dependent on commodity movements.

we have been able to pass on all these changes of coming back to our customers, to rebound to normalize levels from next year quarter to onwards.
So if I talk in terms of the complete financial year, so we stick to our guidance, which we have given earlier, and we will be maintaining it.

adds.what: Ilin fire-affected facility (SFG) resumed; expected fully operational in a couple of months

growth.why: Consumer durables growth guided in line with industry at 20-22% annually, and group reiterated doubling top line in two years, but railway/defence growth was cut to 15-20%; Sidwal Greenfield plant runs at only ~40% utilisation, Hosur PCB expansion is due H1 CY27 and Korea expansion CY28, with FY27 capex of ₹1,800-2,000 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consumer durables margin recovery expected from Q3 as remaining 50% of Q2 commodity increase passes to customers, but FY27 still carries 50-100 bps margin hit and normalised RAC EBITDA margin is now 14-16% vs earlier 19-20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ascent Circuits Hosur PCB expansion due to start by H1 CY27 and Ilin SFG fully operational in about a couple of months; Korea circuit expansion follows in CY28, with Sidwal Greenfield already running at only ~40% utilisation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consumer durables growth guided in line with industry at 20-22% for the year (H1 industry 18%), and electronics revenue grew 94% to ₹1,248 crore in Q2, though RAC volume growth was not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of ₹1,800-2,000 crore is already committed with a similar range in FY28, so further capex is expected to follow the Hosur and Korea expansions, though no new specific project was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Railway/defence FY27 growth was cut to 15-20% from earlier expectations and consumer durables margin hit of 50-100 bps was held, leaving little room for an upgrade beyond the reiterated doubling-of-top-line goal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Railway offtake delays already forced a cut, and consumer durables margins depend on commodity levels staying at H1 levels, with further spikes flagged as a suppressant.

rows.label: Legacy fixed-price contracts repricing
rows.why: Legacy fixed-price contracts without price variation clauses are a margin drag in RAC and railways, and new contracts are being negotiated at new commodity levels, with about 12% commodity inflation vs ~8% blended price increase in Q2.

rows.label: Ilin IPO and stake dilution
rows.when: IPO window within about 1 year; CB approval in 3-4 months
rows.why: Management says ultimate dilution could be below 40% while Amber expects to keep above 51% control, but the DRHP restricts disclosure and timing is not firm.

rows.label: PCB/CCL shortage easing
rows.why: Management expects the PCB/CCL shortage to ease over the next two to three quarters as CCL capacity expands, supporting the electronics ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident on the electronics ramp, doubling-of-revenue target and the pass-through recovery from Q3, but evasive on electronics organic split, PCB vs EMS revenue, volumes and IPO questions citing the DRHP; analysts pushed on consumer durables margins and the commodity pass-through.
